newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Sibneft to handle own crude oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Russian Sibneft to handle own crude oil exports.

text.p: Russian oil mini-major Sibneft said on Monday it would handle its own oil exports from April.

Company spokesman Fillip Murashov said vertically-integrated Sibneft, which accounts for 4.7 percent of Russia's total crude oil exports, would set up a sales section but did not say how it would market output to Western traders or refiners.
Sibneft, whose crude oil production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz, exported an average 86,800 barrels per day, or bpd, in 1996, from output of 372,200 bpd.
An average 58,760 bpd were exported through KomiTEK-Moscow, 18,100 bpd through Rosnefteimpex, 8,905 bpd through Balkar-Trading and 1,108 bpd through Alfa-Eko.
Sibneft said all its exports would go to non-Commonwealth of Independence States customers.
